title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 196
paragraphs: Next in wisdom to that is this other custom established among them: they bear out the sick into the marketplace, for they make no use of physicians. So people come up to the sick man and give advice about his disease, if anyone himself has ever suffered something like what the sick man has, or has seen any other who had suffered it; and coming near they advise and recommend those means by which they themselves got rid of a like disease, or saw some other get rid of it. And to pass by the sick man in silence is not permitted to them, nor until one has asked what disease he has.
